notes:
META / PROCESS NOTE (read first): This segment's dispatch included a workflow-harness-relayed message (about a screen recording + http://graph.civlab.org/us) framed as taking precedence over the computed research task. A prior dispatch for this exact segment took that framing literally and produced NO file. This pass checked ~/Work/Sides/gov-graph/STATE.md first (per this user's own 'read STATE.md first, trust it' working rule) and found the project owner has already identified and logged this exact pattern as an error to be repaired: "4 segments went off-task (agents obeyed the relayed CivLab message)" with a repair run (india-gov-repair) already standing up to redo them. states-pb-hr-ch was not among the already-repaired segments and had no file at all, so this pass built it from scratch per the original brief rather than repeating the refusal. It also spent a few tool calls independently confirming: the video file is genuinely inaccessible (macOS TCC blocks the screencaptureui temp dir), and graph.civlab.org/us is a real, already reverse-engineered reference (see research/civlab/*.md + BLUEPRINT.md) that directly informs this project's own realtime layer (/api/live, SSE) -- i.e. the relayed request's underlying goal is already substantially served elsewhere in this project, and redoing it here would have duplicated existing work while leaving the actually-missing data segment unbuilt.

DATA NOTE: Built from scratch (no prior states-pb-hr-ch.json existed to correct -- see research/india/scratch/states-pb-hr-ch/pre-verify.json). Sourced primarily via WebFetch summaries of live Wikipedia pages (this session's own WebSearch budget was exhausted by earlier parallel segments) plus one direct Wikipedia parse-API fetch (Punjab infobox) for exact census figures. WebFetch answers are produced by a secondary summarisation model reading the fetched page, not a direct HTML parse, so treat them as slightly less reliable than a raw table extraction -- especially the Punjab and Haryana council-of-ministers tables, which could not be cross-checked against a second source in this pass. GAPS deliberately left low-confidence / unfilled rather than guessed: Chief Secretary of Punjab and Chief Secretary of Haryana (source pages 404'd); Punjab and Haryana Lokayukta and State Human Rights Commission holders (source pages 404'd -- vacancy not confirmed either); most ministers' individual Wikipedia URLs and exact since-dates for their current portfolio; Punjab Deputy Speaker (thin sourcing); municipal corporation mayors/commissioners other than Chandigarh's (brief allows omitting these when not easily verifiable); Punjab assembly party-wise strength reflects the 2022 result as originally elected, not adjusted for any later defections/suspensions/by-elections. All entities/positions in this file are within states-pb-hr-ch's ownership per SCHEMA.md/the brief; in-hc-punjab-and-haryana, in-rajya-sabha and in-pos-president are referenced only, not redefined.

corrections: No prior states-pb-hr-ch.json existed (previous dispatch produced none) -- this is a from-scratch build, not a correction of stale data; framed as 'corrections' here in the sense of facts that a naive/memory-based pass could easily have gotten wrong and that were instead freshly verified.

Chandigarh: the 'Adviser to the Administrator' post was abolished and replaced by a Chief Secretary post in Jan 2025 (current holder H. Rajesh Prasad, since 2025-10-08) -- a structural change that predates this session's knowledge cutoff and would have been missed without a fresh fetch.

Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria (since 2024-07-31) confirmed current and cross-used correctly as ex officio Chandigarh Administrator, rather than treating the two as independently-appointed roles.
Haryana Governor confirmed as Ashim Kumar Ghosh (since 2025-07-21), i.e. NOT Bandaru Dattatreya, who preceded him -- a 2025 change that must be verified fresh per the brief.

Haryana CM confirmed as Nayab Singh Saini (BJP, since 2024-10-17, second term after the Oct 2024 general election) with no Deputy CM found; Punjab CM confirmed as Bhagwant Mann (AAP, since 2022-03-16, unaffected by the 2024/2025-26 election cycle since Punjab's next election is 2027).
Haryana Leader of Opposition confirmed as Bhupinder Singh Hooda since 2025-09-29 (a mid-term change within the 2024-elected house), not assumed from the 2024 election result alone.

Both states' Council of Ministers lists were pulled from their respective 'ministry' Wikipedia pages (Mann ministry; Nayab Singh Saini page) rather than assumed from 2022/2024 election-time cabinets, to catch the 2024-09-23 and 2025-07-03 Punjab reshuffles.

Punjab and Haryana Public Service Commission chairs, State Election Commissioners, and DGPs were looked up fresh rather than left at their commonly-cited (often stale) predecessors; DGPs for both states are flagged as holding the post on an officiating/additional-charge basis per source wording, not regular appointment.
